key_insight: Pretraining strongly determines how much reinforcement learning can improve reasoning, and RL changes models by revealing or amplifying correct behaviors rather than simply sharpening existing ones.
engineering_relevance: For LLM training pipelines, pretraining data and scale should be treated as first-class design variables because they predict downstream RL efficiency and final reasoning performance.
method: Pretrained 5M–1B parameter language models on human chess games.
Applied supervised fine-tuning on synthetic reasoning traces.
Ran RL on chess puzzles with verifiable rewards, then tested transfer on 1B math-domain text models.
evidence_signal: Across compute sweeps, post-RL performance was predicted by pretraining loss, RL reward slope scaled roughly linearly with pretraining tokens, and the pattern also held in a math-text transfer experiment.
watch_item: Chess provides a controlled testbed, but its controlled rewards and domain structure may not fully capture the noise, diversity, and evaluation challenges of real-world LLM reasoning tasks.
paper_title: Understanding Reasoning from Pretraining to Post-Training
